title: Data Schemas
markdown:
The shapes below are the load-bearing data structures: episodic SQLite tables (in `episodic_memory.db`) and the Pydantic models for departments and people.

### Episodic tables

| Table | Key columns |
|---|---|
| `decisions` | `id`, `timestamp`, `domain`, `summary`, `rationale`, `outcome`, `tags`, `department`, `session_id` |
| `initiatives` | `id`, `title`, `status`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `summary`, `department` |
| `advice_given` | `id`, `timestamp`, `domain`, `query_summary`, `advice_summary`, `department`, `session_id` |
| `facts` | `id`, `kind` (fact / correction / profile), `subject`, `subject_key`, `statement`, `previous_statement`, `source_quote`, `source_channel`, `session_id`, `turn_id`, `recorded_by_person_id`, `created_at`, `status` (active / superseded / retired), `superseded_by`, `retired_at`, `retired_reason` |
| `scheduled_actions` | `id`, `created_at`, `run_at`, `channel`, `channel_ref`, `intent_text`, `status`, `attempts`, `kind`, `department`, `assigned_to_person_id`, `awaiting_response_since`, `scope_key`, `required_scope` |
| `outbound_context` | `id`, `created_at`, `channel`, `channel_ref`, `recipient_person_id`, `outbound_text`, `originating_session_id`, `outbound_message_id`, `consumed_at`, `status` |
| `history_reminders` | (`person_id`, `day`) PK, `sent_at` — the days a person was reminded of notes due (`memory.history_reminders`), older days pruned on write |
| `session_drive_files` | (`session_id`, `person_id`, `file_id`) PK, `name`, `mime_type`, `link`, `summary` (first 600 chars of an opened file), `opened`, `found_by` (the search query), `first_seen_at`, `last_seen_at` — Drive files a conversation found or opened (`memory.drive_reads`) |
| `session_drive_searches` | `id`, `session_id`, `person_id`, `query`, `result_count`, `searched_at` — every Drive search a conversation ran |
| `saved_tools` | `name` (PK), `description`, `enabled`, `current_version`, `created_at`, `updated_at` — scripts the Executive saved to run again (`workflows.saved_tools`) |
| `saved_tool_versions` | (`name`, `version`) PK, `description`, `script`, `tools` (JSON: the tools the script called when saved), `origin` (`chat` or `workflow:<name>/<step>`), `created_at` |
| `saved_tool_runs` | `id`, `name`, `version`, `ok`, `calls`, `duration_ms`, `origin`, `at` — the newest 200 runs per tool |
| `chat_messages` | `id`, `session_id`, `role`, `content`, `created_at`, `action_chips`, `stopped`, `sender_person_id`, `feedback`, `feedback_note`, `feedback_by_person_id`, `sources` (JSON `{sources: [{kind, title, url}], unavailable: [area]}` — what an assistant reply looked at and which areas it left out; NULL on older rows) |
| `attunement_usage` | `day` (PK, UTC date), `calls` — the per-day ceiling on open-loop extraction model calls |
| `attunement_profiles` | `person_id` (PK), `rules` (JSON: up to 4 `{text, basis, evidence}`), `locked`, `updated_at`, `updated_by`, `last_pass_at`, `pass_day`, `passes_today`, `last_message_id` — per-person working style plus pass pacing |
| `attunement_profile_history` | `id`, `person_id`, `created_at`, `rules`, `locked`, `updated_by` — every change to a working style |
| `proactive_outcomes` | `id`, `created_at`, `person_id`, `source`, `ref`, `channel`, `channel_ref`, `outbound_context_id`, `outcome` (`replied` / `acted` / `ignored` / `void`, NULL while open), `resolved_at` — one row per proactive DM (Attunement outcome ledger) |
| `delegation_settings` | `person_id` (PK), `enabled` (default 0), `updated_at`, `updated_by` — Act as me, per person; no row means off |
| `history_notes` | `id`, `person_id`, `visibility` (`private`), `source` (`approved_reply`), `channel` (`email`), `conversation_key` (a hash of the channel and thread, never the thread id), `counterpart`, `subject`, `kind` (`promised` / `agreed` / `declined` / `answered` / `asked` / `shared`), `summary`, `quote` (the person's own words), `due_date`, `trust`, `occurred_at`, `created_at`, `expires_at` (NULL: until forgotten), `pinned`, `correction`, `corrected_at`, `kept_from` (when the retention clock started: NULL means `occurred_at`; an unpin restarts it) — Always in the loop, one row per note |
| `history_settings` | `id` (1), `retention_days` (NULL: until forgotten; no row means 90), `updated_at`, `updated_by` — the company retention |
| `history_person_settings` | `person_id` (PK), `reply_notes` (default 0), `retention_days` (NULL: the company's), `updated_at`, `updated_by` |
| `history_excluded` | `person_id`, `conversation_key` (PK together), `created_at` — conversations a person asked not to remember |
| `history_chat_passes` | `person_id`, `day` (PK together, UTC `YYYY-MM-DD`), `passes` — note passes run on a person's chat messages that day, against the daily cap; older days pruned on write |
| `delegation_voice` | `person_id` (PK), `profile` (JSON: `greetings` per audience, `sign_off`, `signature`, `length`, `formality`, up to 8 `habits`, up to 6 `avoid`, up to 3 `exemplars`), `locked`, `learned_at`, `sample_count`, `updated_at`, `updated_by` — "How I write" |
| `delegation_voice_history` | `id`, `person_id`, `created_at`, `profile`, `locked`, `updated_by` — every change to a writing profile |
| `delegation_drafts` | `id`, `person_id`, `source` (`chat` \| `inbox`), `thread_id`, `draft_id`, `message_id`, `sent_message_id`, `created_at` — one row of ids per draft Act as me saved in someone's Gmail (no address, subject or text): the daily limit counts it, and "How I write" skips a chat draft's thread and a sent draft's message |
| `delegation_inbox_watch` | `person_id` (PK), `enabled`, `watch_since` (reset on every off→on), `last_poll_at`, `status`, `backoff_until`, `failures`, `updated_at`, `updated_by` — **Draft replies to my inbox**, per person; no row means off |
| `delegation_inbox_messages` | `id`, `person_id`, `message_id`, `thread_id`, `received_at`, `sender_key` (a hash of the address, never the address), `relation`, `outcome` (`processing`, `retry` — left for a later scan, `skipped`, `not_needed`, `deferred`, `failed`, `drafted`, `sent`, `dismissed`, `closed`, `expired`), `reason`, `classified`, `attempts`, `draft_id`, `decision_id`, `flags` (JSON), `created_at`, `updated_at`; `UNIQUE(person_id, message_id)` — the inbox watcher's cursor: what happened to each message it looked at |
| `delegation_handle_it` | `person_id` (PK), `enabled`, `mode` (`careful`, `balanced` or `bold`), `levels` (the per-kind setting `mode` replaced, kept for older rows), `updated_at`, `updated_by` — **Handle it for me**, per person; no row means off |
| `delegation_handled` | `id`, `person_id`, `thread_id`, `decision_id`, `sent_message_id`, `sent_at`; index on `(person_id, sent_at)` — one row per reply or follow-up Handle it for me sent on its own, read for its one-per-thread-a-day and daily limits |

| `dynamic_workflows` | `name` (PK), `definition` (JSON of `DynamicWorkflowDef`), `is_active`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `owner_person_id` (creator; set on insert only, kept out of the definition JSON) |
| `workflow_approved_targets` | (`workflow_name`, `value`) PK, `key`, `approved_at`, `run_id` — targets a workflow's tool steps may write to without asking again; cleared when the workflow is deleted |
| `executive_control` | `id` (PK, always 1), `paused`, `paused_at`, `paused_by`, `reason`, `updated_at` — the operator pause switch (`scheduler.pause`); operator-level, so client-slot switches carry it across |
| `app_migrations` | `name` (PK), `applied_at` — one-shot data migrations (sweeps that must run exactly once per DB); schema DDL stays idempotent and is not recorded here |

`department` and `session_id` are additive columns (default `''`); `session_id` scopes per-thread recall. `scheduled_actions.status` ∈ pending / running / done / failed / cancelled, and `scheduled_actions.kind` includes `dynamic_workflow` (a cadence-fired user-created workflow run) and `open_loop` (an Attunement open loop: `assigned_to_person_id` is the owner, `awaiting_response_since` the due time — cleared when the loop closes — and `scope_key` `loop:{owner}:{hash}`, unique among open loops via the partial index `idx_scheduled_open_loop_scope`). `chat_messages.sender_person_id` is the resolved rostered sender of a user message (never the session owner's principal fallback; NULL on legacy rows and for unrostered senders); `feedback` is `up` / `down` on an assistant reply. `dynamic_workflows` stores user-created (dynamic) workflow definitions interpreted by the generic `DynamicWorkflow` engine; the JSON `definition` holds free-text input fields and an ordered step list (specialist / approval_gate / synthesis) plus an optional cadence.

### Legacy tables (talent / staff onboarding)

The talent (executive-search) and staff-onboarding features were removed. Their tables —
`engagements`, `candidates`, `offers`, `onboarding_templates`, `onboarding_plans`,
`onboarding_tasks` — are **not dropped**: no code creates, reads or writes them any more,
but rows survive on upgraded installs. `clients.slots` still wipes them when a blank client
slot is activated (existence-guarded, a no-op on fresh installs) so a slot can never inherit
a previous client's candidate data.

### Department / Goal / ChecklistItem

| Model | Fields |
|---|---|
| `DepartmentConfig` | `slug`, `title`, `specialist_key`, `charter`, `authority_level`, `head_person_id`, `head_persona_slug`, `cadences`, `slack_channel_id`, `discord_channel_id`, `telegram_chat_id` |
| `Goal` | `id`, `department_slug`, `period_type`, `period_value`, `key_result`, `target`, `current`, `status`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `last_reviewed_at` |
| `DepartmentState` | `config`, `goals`, `headcount`, `budget_usd`, `member_person_ids`, `updated_at` |

`authority_level` ∈ `auto_execute` / `propose_only` / `escalate`; `Goal.status` ∈ `on_track` / `at_risk` / `off_track`.

### Person

| Field group | Fields |
|---|---|
| Identity | `id`, `full_name`, `role`, `is_principal`, `kind`, `department_slugs` |
| Contact | `email`, `email_aliases`, `slack_user_id`, `telegram_chat_id`, `discord_user_id`, `preferred_channel` |
| Routing | `availability`, `authority_scope`, `response_sla_hours`, `on_leave_until`, `reports_to_person_id` |
| Lifecycle | `archived`, `created_at`, `updated_at` |

Exactly one `Person` should have `is_principal=True` — the fallback approver when no delegated person matches.

`kind` is `team` (the default) or `contact` — someone outside the team, such as a client or contractor. It is an additive column, `kind TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'team'`, added by the same `PRAGMA table_info`-guarded migration as `discord_user_id`, so every existing row is a team member. The principal is always `team`: the store refuses to write a principal contact (`PrincipalContactError`), and `initialize_db` repairs a hand-edited one on boot. A stored value the code does not know reads as `contact`. Every roster read in `people.store` and `people.registry` returns team members only unless it passes `include_contacts=True` (see Org).

`email` is the one address a person signs in with; `email_aliases` (read from the `person_emails` table, up to 10) are other addresses they write from — they match inbound mail and may be emailed, but never sign in (see Org).

### People-side tables

These live next to `people` (created by `people.store.initialize_db`, which also runs `people.roster_requests.initialize_tables`):

| Table | Key columns |
|---|---|
| `person_emails` | `id`, `person_id` (FK → `people`, `ON DELETE CASCADE`), `email`, `email_norm` (trimmed + lowercased, **UNIQUE** across the roster), `source` (`manual` / `chat_tool` / `roster_request`), `roster_request_id`, `created_at` — a person's aliases; deleted when they are archived |
| `roster_requests` | `id`, `channel` (`email` / `slack` / `discord` / `telegram`), `channel_ref` (the address or chat id), `display_name` (sanitised, unverified), `profile_email`, `on_company_domain`, `suggested_kind`, `suggested_person_id`, `status` (`pending` / `resolving` / `approved` / `linked` / `declined` / `expired` / `superseded`), `resolved_person_id`, `resolved_kind`, `resolved_via` (`web` / `slack` / `discord` / `telegram` / `email` / `people_page`), `resolved_at`, `token_hash` (the email answer token, hashed; cleared on resolve), `confirm_message_id`, `notified_at`, `notified_channel`, `ack_sent_at`, `alert_id`, `message_count`, `first_seen_at`, `last_seen_at`, `expires_at` — one pending row per `(channel, channel_ref)` (partial unique index) |
| `roster_request_messages` | `id`, `request_id` (FK, cascade), `external_id` (unique per request, so a redelivery is held once), `payload_json` (what the adapter needs to replay it), `preview`, `received_at`, `replay_status` (`held` / `replaying` / `replayed` / `dropped` / `failed` / `unavailable`), `replayed_at` — at most 10 per request; `payload_json` and `preview` are blanked once a message is replayed or dropped |
| `roster_ack_log` | `id`, `channel`, `channel_ref`, `sent_at` — one row per acknowledgement sent to a new sender, for the per-sender window and the daily cap |

**Take the lead tables** (`orchestrator.take_the_lead`, created on first use, per company in `clients.slots` and `reset_all_state`): `take_the_lead` (`scope` PK: `executive` or `person:<id>`, `enabled`, `updated_at`, `updated_by`; each kind's Ask first is a `decision_class_state` row for `take_the_lead_action:<kind>`); `take_the_lead_rules` (`id`, `scope`: `company` or `person:<id>`, `kind` person|domain|words|amount, `value`, `created_by`, `created_at`); `take_the_lead_log` (`id`, `at`, `scope`, `source` reflection|research|scheduled, `tool`, `summary`, `status` done|waiting|approved|declined|failed, `why`, `decision_id`). A held action is a `decision_instances` row of class `take_the_lead_action` whose payload carries the tool, its input, whether it is an MCP tool, the gate kind or rule, the reason and the summary.
